title: What Neuromorphic Computing Chips Is
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Neuromorphic computing chips are processors that compute the way brains do: networks of artificial neurons communicating with sparse electrical spikes instead of dense clocked arithmetic. Memory and processing sit together in each neuron, so there is no shuttling data back and forth — the pattern that burns most of the energy in conventional chips. This record is the entry point of the teaching ladder for Neuromorphic Computing Chips: start here, then move through the research state, the specifications, the public developments, the open challenges, and finally each piece needed to build it.
key_points: Neuromorphic Computing Chips in one line: Neuromorphic computing chips are processors that compute the way brains do: networks of artificial neurons communicating with sparse electrical spikes instead of dense clocked arithmetic.
Why it matters: They promise orders-of-magnitude better energy efficiency for AI workloads like sensing, pattern recognition, and robotics..
Where it is used: always-on sensors, robotics, edge AI, brain-computer interfaces, and scientific computing..
Ladder rank 1 — the foundation. Everything else builds on this.

t: Current Research State of Neuromorphic Computing Chips
title: Current Research State of Neuromorphic Computing Chips
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Intel's Loihi 2 (1M neurons), IBM's NorthPole, and BrainChip's Akida have demonstrated spike-based inference at milliwatt power. Research focuses on on-chip learning (STDP, surrogate gradients), scaling to billions of synapses, and programming models. The gap: training large neuromorphic networks still lags GPUs, and software toolchains are immature. Research moves in three waves: laboratory proof of concept, scaled prototypes under controlled conditions, and field trials. Neuromorphic Computing Chips currently sits at the stage described above, and the pieces records show what each wave still needs.
key_points: State of play: Intel's Loihi 2 (1M neurons), IBM's NorthPole, and BrainChip's Akida have demonstrated spike-based inference at milliwatt power.
Leading approaches: digital spiking cores (Loihi), analog in-memory (NorthPole), event-based vision+compute (Akida), memristor synapses.
Key institutions and programs: Intel, IBM, BrainChip, SynSense, university neuromorphic labs.
What would change the timeline: the challenges record lists the blockers.
